sources.note: Read 2026-11-11 in a text extraction of the Louisiana copy (the extractor did not keep every table column, so placement was checked against the course's own reading of 2026-11-09 in ems-sources.ts). EMR: CPR and AED, tourniquet and wound packing, naloxone, oral airway, BVM, oxygen; no pulse oximetry, glucose monitoring, epinephrine auto-injector or transport. EMT adds pulse oximetry, glucose monitoring, epinephrine auto-injector, aspirin, oral glucose, CPAP, 12-lead acquisition (not interpretation), transport. AEMT adds IV and IO access, non-medicated IV fluids, supraglottic airways and a limited list of IV and IM medications including dextrose and glucagon. Paramedic adds 12-lead interpretation, manual defibrillation, intubation and the wider formulary. No newer model was found 2026-11-11 (EMS.gov's page was unavailable; the only other 'update' found is the 2017 change notice adding tourniquets, wound packing and naloxone to EMR and EMT).

brief.situation: 06:10. You are the paramedic on an ALS ambulance with an EMT partner. Mr. Kowalski, 61, about 90 kg, woke at 05:30 with crushing central chest pressure going into his jaw; he is sweating and nauseated. His wife called 911.
handover: Region's STEMI plan (authored for this case): a STEMI identified in the field goes directly to a PCI center with the cath lab activated from the field, if first-contact-to-device can be met within 90 minutes.
University Hospital (24/7 PCI) is 28 minutes away. Lakeside Community Hospital (no PCI; fibrinolysis, then transfer) is 8 minutes away.
Full paramedic scope: 12-lead interpretation, IV, aspirin, nitroglycerin, fentanyl, fluids, manual defibrillation.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated seconds per real second. Pause any time.
First medical contact is 06:10. Scene time, the drive and the hospital's readiness all add up on the clock until the artery is opened.
Partway through you are asked to explain your decisions in writing. The case ends at the hospital door, then a debrief scores what you did.

source.note: Ten electrodes and a 12-lead acquisition: about 1 min.
IV access: about 90 s.
A cuff cycle: about 30 s.
Stair chair down one flight, onto the cot and loaded: about 4 min.
To University Hospital: about 28 min (authored).
To Lakeside: about 8 min (authored).

why.question: What did the 12-lead show and what did you do with it, and why give or withhold nitroglycerin?

parts.label: ECG and the system
parts.criteria: 12-lead within 10 minutes of contact; ST elevation in II, III, aVF with reciprocal depression in I and aVL is an inferior STEMI; transmit and activate the cath lab at a PCI center within 10 minutes of the ECG; go to the PCI center (28 minutes) because first contact to device can still be under 90 minutes, which the non-PCI hospital cannot offer.
parts.modelAnswer: The 12-lead at a few minutes showed ST elevation in II, III and aVF with reciprocal depression in I and aVL: an inferior STEMI. I transmitted it and activated the cath lab at University right away, and went there directly, since first contact to device stays under 90 minutes; Lakeside would mean lytics and a transfer.

parts.label: Nitrates and pain
parts.criteria: Ask about phosphodiesterase inhibitors; tadalafil 8 hours ago means no nitrates (within 48 hours), and RV involvement adds risk; aspirin 162-325 mg chewed; oxygen only if hypoxic; pads on; IV; opioid analgesia (fentanyl) instead, watching the pressure; treat hypotension with fluid boluses.
parts.modelAnswer: He took tadalafil 8 hours ago, so nitroglycerin is contraindicated, and the inferior STEMI with V4R elevation makes him preload dependent anyway. Aspirin 324 chewed, pads on, IV, no oxygen at 96%, and fentanyl for the pain while watching his pressure; if it falls, small saline boluses.

expertPath.text: Monitor and 12-lead at once while your partner gets the history. Inferior STEMI with reciprocal changes.
Transmit and activate University's cath lab. Aspirin 324 chewed. Ask about PDE inhibitors: tadalafil 8 hours ago, so no nitroglycerin. V4R: RV involvement.
Pads on, IV, BP 116/74; no oxygen at 96%. Fentanyl 50 mcg for the pain, watching the pressure.
Load and go to University (28 min); fentanyl repeat if needed; saline 250 mL if the pressure falls. First contact to device about 65 minutes.

vf.headline: VF after a pressure crash
vf.body: Nitroglycerin within 48 hours of tadalafil, in a preload-dependent inferior STEMI, can collapse the pressure. Ask the question, withhold the nitrate, and answer any fall with saline boluses.

cathLab.headline: Straight to the cath lab
cathLab.body: A fast 12-lead, a field activation, aspirin, the nitrate withheld for the right reason, pain treated, a short scene and the PCI center: the system of care working as designed.

pciGaps.headline: PCI center, with gaps
pciGaps.body: Check the 12-lead time, whether the cath lab was activated from the field, the scene time, and the nitrate decision.

nonPci.headline: No PCI at the door
nonPci.body: With first contact to device achievable within 90 minutes at University, a field-identified STEMI goes there directly with the cath lab activated.

scoring.modelReasoning: Chest pressure with diaphoresis needs a 12-lead within 10 minutes of first contact. ST elevation in II, III and aVF with reciprocal depression in I and aVL is an inferior STEMI: transmit and activate the cath lab at a PCI center within 10 minutes of the ECG, and go there directly when first contact to device can be kept under 90 minutes. Aspirin 162-325 mg chewed; oxygen only if hypoxic; pads on; IV. Always ask about phosphodiesterase inhibitors: tadalafil within 48 hours rules out nitrates, and RV involvement (V4R) makes him preload dependent. Treat pain with an opioid such as fentanyl while watching the pressure, and treat hypotension with small saline boluses. Keep the scene short.

leads.ask: While the 12-lead prints: which pattern means an inferior STEMI?

choices.label: ST elevation in II, III, aVF with depression in I and aVL
ST elevation in I, aVL, V5-V6

leads.explain: II, III and aVF look at the inferior wall; reciprocal depression in I and aVL supports the diagnosis. III higher than II suggests the right coronary artery, often with RV involvement.

choices.label: A 250 mL saline bolus and recheck

pressure.explain: NASEMSO: be ready to respond to hypotension with a fluid bolus. An RV infarct is preload dependent; nitrates and more opioid lower preload further.
